blocks.text:
**Group departure:** 5–16 February  

## About the trip

Carnival is the focus of the first part of this journey. At the Sambadrome, you will watch samba schools perform among enormous moving floats, elaborate costumes and dancing that continues until morning. By day, Corcovado and Sugar Loaf reveal Rio from above, showing how the city fits between the ocean, bays, Tijuca Forest and steep hillsides.

After Rio, the route takes you to Iguazu Falls. The Brazilian side offers sweeping views of the cascades, while the Argentine side brings you close to the water along raised walkways. The roar at the Devil’s Throat, the humid air and the constant spray feel quite different from what photographs can convey.

In the Amazon, rivers and forest replace city streets. You will walk through the jungle with a naturalist guide, discover local daily life, see the flooded igapó forest, try piranha fishing and head out on an evening walk with torches. If you wish, you can add the Meeting of the Waters, where the Rio Negro and Solimões meet, and swimming with pink river dolphins.

The final days are spent in Búzios. There is no compulsory sightseeing programme here: choose a beach, take a boat out to sea, explore the peninsula by buggy or simply spend the day beside the ocean.

Over 12 days, the programme moves through several different settings, making the transfers as important as the excursions. Each busy stretch leads naturally into the next: Rio gives way to Iguazu, followed by the Amazon’s rivers, before the journey ends on the coast. This sequence lets you experience the country through a variety of activities and landscapes.

## Optional excursions

In Rio, you can book the Roxy Show with dinner and private transfers ($260), Cook in Rio ($250), a Pedra Bonita hike ($202), a cycling tour ($250) and a private 30-minute helicopter flight with transfer and guide ($641 per person).

In Iguazu, options include Macuco Safari ($130), the Bird Park ($50) and a private 35-minute flight over the falls and national park ($3,666 per helicopter for 1–5 people). In the Amazon, you can add the Meeting of the Waters ($150) and swimming with pink river dolphins ($100).
